transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I basically spend most of my day going back over the exact same things in my house. The outlets, the locks, my tools, even the dust. I just keep checking and fixing them, again and again. I do it until I'm completely worn out, but I still don't feel sure enough to just... leave it alone.
Do you find that you have certain thoughts or worries that keep coming back and feel like you have to do these checking or fixing rituals to make them go away?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Even when I know I did a job right, these... ugly thoughts just keep jumping into my head. Like, I'll start worrying that a loose wire I missed is going to spark and burn the whole house down. Or maybe a nail I left somewhere is going to end up hurting my wife. I try to push them out of my mind, I really do, but... they just come right back stronger. And I can't shake it until I go back and check.
Do these unwanted thoughts ever come up when you’re not actively checking things, like when you’re trying to relax or focus on something else?

I'm... not really sure, to be honest. I don't really get much time to just sit and relax. It feels like I'm almost always up doing my rounds, checking things. So I haven't really noticed if they pop up when I'm trying to focus on something else. I just know they're pretty much always in my head until I go fix whatever it is.
When you're not doing your checking routines, do those troubling thoughts ever come up on their own, like when you're trying to rest or concentrate on something else?

Well, like I was just saying... I really couldn't tell you. I don't get much of a chance to rest or concentrate on anything else. If I'm awake, I'm pretty much always up doing my checks. So... I just don't know if they happen during downtime, because I don't really have any downtime to begin with.
Have you ever noticed these troubling thoughts coming up even for a moment when you're not in the middle of checking or fixing things?

I... look, I know you're trying to see if there's even a split second where it happens. But I really just don't have a different answer for you. I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just... my whole day is completely consumed by this. 

From the minute I wake up, I'm on my feet looking at things. There really isn't a single moment where I'm not in the middle of it. So, no, I haven't noticed those thoughts happening outside of my routines, because... well, I don't really have a life outside of them right now.
Have you ever had thoughts come into your mind that aren’t about checking things, but still upset you or felt unwanted, even if just for a moment?

No, not really. Um... everything that upsets me is pretty much tied to the checking. I don't get bad thoughts about other stuff. 

It's just... did I do this right, is that closed, that kind of thing. If I have other thoughts, they don't bother me. It's really just the checking stuff that takes over my head. That's more than enough on its own, honestly.
Are there any other types of thoughts or concerns that make you feel like you have to do something over and over, even if it's not about checking things like outlets or locks?

No, um... no, I don't think so. It's really just the checking. 

I don't have anything else that makes me feel like I need to repeat things. I mean, I don't have to wash my hands a bunch of times or, you know, count things or anything like that. It's just making sure things are off, or closed, or safe. That's the only thing that gets me stuck doing it over and over.
